tweet.text:
“I shall suppose, then, not that God who is supremely good and the source of truth, but some evil demon of the utmost power and cunning has employed all his energies in order to deceive me. I shall think that the sky, the air, the earth, colors, shapes, sounds and all external things are merely the delusions of dreams which he has devised to ensnare my judgment. I shall consider myself as not having hands or eyes, or flesh, or blood or senses, but as falsely believing that I have all these things.”

Descartes is not claiming such a demon exists. He is saying that if it is even possible, then he cannot be certain of anything based on the senses or even pure reason.

That is, until he finds something the demon cannot touch.

“Cogito ergo sum”
